method: Each map panel is registered to the modern LHA linework (coast, provincial border and LHA edges). Printed city dots or provincial corners give a starting position. An iterative closest-point fit then matches every sampled source boundary point to the nearest modern edge, rejecting matches beyond a shrinking distance threshold, and fits an affine, then quadratic, then cubic polynomial. Main maps add a smoothed thin-plate spline for local distortion. Insets are registered separately.
accuracy: Distances are from each registered source boundary point to the nearest modern LHA edge or coastline. "heldOut" refits the panel without one quarter of the map (a checkerboard of 25-point blocks) and measures those unseen blocks. Source generalization (a 1:10-million-scale drawing) is part of the residual.

regions.name: Simon Fraser
regions.note: New Westminster is too small to resolve on the 1997/98 inset. The 2001 boundary schedule for this region names Burnaby and New Westminster, and the Statistics Canada map places New Westminster in Simon Fraser.

regions.name: Capital
regions.note: The Southern Gulf Islands are shaded but unnumbered in the inset. The 2001 boundary schedule runs Capital's edge along Houstoun Passage and Stuart Channel, which places Salt Spring and the southern Gulf Islands inside it.
